examples.en: I usually have lunch with my friends on weekends.
If you have time, would you like to have dinner together?
I'm glad we get to do this project together.

explain: 식사, 시간, 여행, 인생처럼 무언가를 함께 누릴 때 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '같이 먹어요'처럼 풀어 쓰는 게 더 자연스럽고, '같이하다'는 '식사를 같이하다'처럼 조금 격식 있게 들려요. '함께하다'도 비슷한데 더 격식 있는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Friends who share my goals gathered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 목표가 같아서 한편이 된다는 뜻이에요. 연설이나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people hold the same goal or view and stand together. Common in speeches and writing.

explain_en: It fits things you share or enjoy together: meals, time, trips, a life. In casual speech people just say '같이 먹어요' (eat together); '같이하다' sounds a little more polite, as in '식사를 같이하다'. '함께하다' is similar but more formal.

dis.h: do or spend something together with someone
gh: split a cost or duty among people

p.n: 공유하다 needs something to share (info, files); it can't mean doing an activity together.

t90.ax: I'm glad we get to do this project together.

examples.en: In summer the rain goes on for over a week.
The meeting went on for three hours.

examples.ko: 이 더위는 다음 주에도 계속될 거예요.
examples.en: This heat will continue next week too.
I'm so tired from the nonstop overtime.
My cough kept going for days, so I went to the hospital.
The two people's conversation continued until night.

explain: '계속하다'는 사람이 이어 가는 것이고, '계속되다'는 일이 저절로 이어지는 것이에요. 비·더위·기침·야근처럼 내가 멈추기 어려운 일에 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '계속 공부해요'처럼 '계속'만 부사로 붙여 쓰는 경우가 훨씬 많아요.

phrases.en: The hot weather is continuing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 이어지는 중이라는 뜻이에요. 날씨 이야기에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is still going on now; common when talking about weather.

phrases.en: If your cough continues, go to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 계속 이어질 때의 조건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)면 to give a condition: if it keeps going.

phrases.en: I'm having a hard time because of the continuing heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 이어지는 일을 꾸며 말해요. 더위·비·추위 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -는 to describe something that keeps going; common with heat, rain, or cold.

explain_en: '계속하다' is when a person keeps something going; '계속되다' is when something just keeps going by itself. It fits things you can't easily stop: rain, heat, a cough, overtime. In everyday speech, '계속' alone as an adverb ('계속 공부해요') is far more common.

dis.h: go on without stopping; has no object
gh: keep doing something; needs an object
continue by linking to what came before
formal; keep existing, like an institution

p.n: 이어지다 stresses linking to what came before.

t90.ax: The meeting went on for three hours.

examples.en: This company advertises its new product on TV.
We're advertising our small bakery online.
That actor advertised the new cosmetics.
I made flyers to advertise the new restaurant.

examples.ko: 가게를 광고하지 않으면 손님이 안 와요.
examples.en: If you don't advertise the shop, customers won't come.

explain: '광고하다'는 돈을 들여 알리는 느낌이 강하고, '홍보하다'는 돈을 쓰든 안 쓰든 널리 알리는 일을 두루 가리켜요. 친구에게 가게를 알려 주는 건 '소개하다'가 자연스러워요. 'TV 광고', '광고를 보다'처럼 명사 쓰임이 아주 많아요.

phrases.en: We promote the school with a video.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 쓰든 안 쓰든 널리 알리는 일을 두루 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers any effort to spread the word, paid or not.

phrases.en: The new shop is advertising its new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광고하다'와 뜻이 같고, '광고'를 따로 떼어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 광고하다, with 광고 split out as a noun.

phrases.en: I saw an ad for a new movie on the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 보는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who sees the ad.

explain_en: '광고하다' leans toward paid promotion, while '홍보하다' covers spreading the word, paid or not. Telling a friend about a shop is more naturally '소개하다'. The noun is very common: 'TV 광고' (TV ad), '광고를 보다' (watch an ad).

examples.en: In elementary school, I wrote a picture diary every day.
I drew what happened today in my picture diary.

examples.ko: 그림일기는 글솜씨가 없어도 쓸 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: A picture diary is nice because you can write one even without good writing skills.
An old picture diary turned up in the drawer.
I looked back on the day with my child through a picture diary.

explain: 초등학교 저학년 때 방학 숙제나 수업으로 많이 쓰는 일기예요. 어른이 되어 '그림일기를 쓰다'라고 하면 그림으로 하루를 기록한다는 느낌이에요. '일기를 쓰다'와 같이 동사는 '쓰다'를 써요.

phrases.en: When I was little, I wrote a picture diary every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기는 '쓰다'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Diaries go with the verb 쓰다.

phrases.en: We had picture diary homework during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 숙제로 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often comes up as school homework.

phrases.en: I drew a picture of a puppy in my picture diary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기장 안에 그림을 넣는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means putting a drawing inside the diary.

explain_en: This is the kind of diary many children write in lower elementary grades as vacation homework or class work. When an adult says '그림일기를 쓰다', it feels like recording the day with drawings. As with '일기를 쓰다', the verb is '쓰다'.

examples.ko: 새 단어는 단어장에 적어 두고 외워요.
examples.en: I write new words in my vocabulary notebook and memorize them.
I carry my vocabulary notebook in my bag.

examples.ko: 단어장이 거의 다 차서 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: My vocabulary notebook was almost full, so I bought a new one.
My friend's vocabulary notebook is organized really neatly.

explain: 직접 단어를 적는 공책도, 단어를 모아 놓은 책이나 앱 목록도 단어장이라고 해요. '단어장을 만들다', '단어장에 적다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I made a vocabulary notebook before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부할 단어를 직접 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you collect words to study yourself.

phrases.en: I write unfamiliar words in my vocabulary notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단어를 기록해 둘 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for recording words.
phrases.en_equiv: to write in a vocabulary notebook

phrases.en: I memorize words every day with a vocabulary app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰으로 단어를 공부하는 앱을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An app for studying words on a phone.

explain_en: A handwritten notebook of words, or a printed or app-based word list, can all be called 단어장. It goes with '단어장을 만들다' (make one) and '단어장에 적다' (write in one).

examples.en: I tried to climb up the slide but kept slipping.
The playground has swings and a slide.
My younger sibling came down the slide upside down.

examples.ko: 미끄럼틀은 한 명씩 차례대로 타야 해요.
examples.en: You have to take turns going down the slide one at a time.

explain: '미끄럼틀을 타다'가 짝이 되는 표현이에요. '미끄럽다', '미끄러지다'와 소리와 뜻이 가까워서 같이 기억하면 쉬워요. 놀이터에서 그네, 시소와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The children ride the slide at the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미끄럼틀과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 미끄럼틀.

phrases.en: My younger brother came down the slide and laughed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미끄럼틀을 타고 아래로 내려오는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe sliding down from the top.

phrases.en: The playground slide is very tall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 앞에 붙여 어떤 미끄럼틀인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the place in front tells which slide you mean.

explain_en: The natural collocation is '미끄럼틀을 타다'. Its sound and meaning are close to '미끄럽다' and '미끄러지다', so learning them together helps. It often appears with swings and seesaws at playgrounds.

t90.ax: The child came down the slide happily.

examples.en: That village is in the northwest of Seoul.
In winter a cold wind blows in from the northwest.
The small lake is in the northwest of the park.
Dark clouds are rushing in quickly from the northwest.
The compass needle is pointing to the northwest.

explain: 한국의 겨울 찬 바람은 북서쪽에서 오는 일이 많아서 날씨 이야기에 자주 나와요. 'ㄱ' 받침 뒤라서 '서'가 [써]로 세게 소리 나고, [북써쪽]이라고 읽어요. 바람 이름은 '북서풍'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: In winter the northwest wind blows hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북서쪽에서 불어오는 바람을 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for the wind from the northwest.

phrases.en: My school is in the northwest of the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 '에 있다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'e itda' to say where something is.

phrases.en: Go northwest for about an hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'는 가는 방향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Euro' marks the direction you are going.

explain_en: Cold winter winds in Korea often come from the northwest, so this word shows up in weather talk. After the final 'ㄱ' the 'ㅅ' of '서' is tensed, so it is read [buk-sseo-jjok]. The wind itself is called '북서풍'.

t90.ax: That village is in the northwest of Seoul.

examples.en: My stepdad plays with me every weekend.
I cooked together with my stepdad.
Mom and my stepdad got married last year.
Thanks to my stepdad, I got a new family.
I got allowance money from my stepdad.
My stepdad made a delicious dinner for me.

explain: '새아버지'보다 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '새엄마'예요. 서류에서는 '계부'라고 하고, 직접 부를 때는 보통 '아빠'나 '아버지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My mom got married this year, so I got a stepfather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새아빠'와 함께 가족이 새로 생겼을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'saeappa' when a new family member joins the family.

phrases.en: My friend has both a stepfather and a stepmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말 '새엄마'와 함께 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the word with its counterpart 'saeeomma' (stepmother).

phrases.en: My stepfather takes good care of me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새아빠'보다 조금 더 공손하고 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more polite and formal word than 'saeappa'.

explain_en: It is a more casual spoken word than '새아버지'. Its counterpart is '새엄마'. On documents the term is '계부', and when addressing him directly people usually say '아빠' or '아버지'.

t90.ax: I cooked together with my stepdad.

examples.en: There are ten pairs of shoes in the shoe cabinet.
The shoe cabinet next to the entrance is too narrow.
I tidied the shoe cabinet before the guests came.

examples.ko: 새 운동화를 신발장 맨 위 칸에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I put the new sneakers on the top shelf of the shoe cabinet.

examples.ko: 신발장 문이 안 닫혀서 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: The shoe cabinet door won't close, so I need to fix it.

examples.ko: 우리 집 신발장은 우산도 넣을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Our shoe cabinet can hold umbrellas too.

explain: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗기 때문에 대부분 현관 쪽에 신발장이 있어요. 신발을 '넣다, 꺼내다, 정리하다'와 같이 써요. 일상에서는 '신발장'이라고 하면 충분히 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Please put your shoes in the shoe rack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발을 보관할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic expression for storing shoes.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in the shoe rack

phrases.en: I took my sneakers out of the shoe rack.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넣다'의 반대 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the opposite action of 'neota' (to put in).
phrases.en_equiv: to take out of the shoe rack

phrases.en: I tidied up the shoe rack on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발장을 깨끗하게 치우고 정돈할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cleaning and organizing the shoe rack.

explain_en: Korean homes have you take off shoes at the entrance, so the shoe cabinet is usually right there. It goes with verbs like '넣다' (put in), '꺼내다' (take out) and '정리하다' (tidy up). In daily speech, '신발장' is perfectly natural.
